references.text: The ninth commandment forbids false testimony, which is the basis for the prohibition against lying.
The prohibition against lying and deceiving one another reiterates the principle of staying away from falsehood.
A curse on whoever takes a bribe to kill an innocent person, parallel to the prohibition against killing the innocent.
Whoever acquits the guilty and whoever condemns the righteous are both an abomination to the Lord.
A lying tongue is among the things the Lord hates, relating to staying away from lies.
Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who act faithfully are pleasing to him.
Woe to those who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the righteous of justice.
A command not to oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow, and not to shed innocent blood.
The Lord will testify against those who oppress and do not fear him, including those who pervert justice for the righteous.
Judas confesses that he has sinned by betraying innocent blood, showing the consequence of killing the innocent.
Pilate declares himself innocent in this righteous man's blood, a direct reference to the shedding of innocent blood.
Their throat is an open grave; they use their tongue for deceit - relating to the theme of lying speech.
Put away falsehood and speak truth with your neighbor, reiterating the command to stay away from lies.
Do not lie to one another, since you have stripped off the old self with its practices.
Complementary principles for righteous judgments: protection of the innocent (Ex) and equal treatment regardless of status (Lv).
Direct thematic connection within the same legal text concerning false witnesses and protection of the innocent.
Strong thematic parallel regarding justice in court: warning against bribes and protection of the innocent.
General command (do not kill) and its specific legal application to protect the innocent.
Identical to candidate 7; a fundamental command elaborated within a legal context to protect the innocent.
Concrete case study (rape victim) illustrating the principle of not condemning the innocent to death.
